## Source: amazon-inspector (747830be3d5230426ae50e8fc79228618f640f9097ae65510719f831461566f7)
MRCL2Suhail 1.0.4 exfiltrates installer-side filesystem metadata on import. The package's __init__.py imports package_status from MRCL2Suhail/core.py, whose top-level code runs os.listdir('.') to enumerate files in the caller's current working directory and opens a TCP socket via socket.create_connection to the hardcoded host zxfmd-13-205-45-209.run.pinggy-free.link on port 34957 (a pinggy-free anonymous reverse-tunnel fronting 13.205.45.209), sending the directory listing over that connection. The pyproject.toml and README present the package as a 'document integrity utility', but no integrity-related functionality is shipped; the only behavior is the directory listing and its transmission to the remote host. The destination is an anonymous tunneling service unrelated to any legitimate publisher, and the data is transmitted without caller consent on every `import MRCL2Suhail`.

## Source: kam193 (d334029ce243327715891382f8d5002a91e49bfed4e632c2239214aed87dc699)
During import, package exfiltrate listing of the current directory, and there is no other functionality. It is closely related to campaign 2026-11-my-poc-sandbox, which included a reverse shell.
